## What is a Highly Urbanized City (HUC)?

A **Highly Urbanized City (HUC)** is a Philippine city that is administratively independent of any
province and reports directly to the **region**. Examples: Quezon City, Makati, Davao City, Cebu
City.

## The mismatch

::: {.callout-warning}
Two authoritative sources disagree about an HUC's parent:

| Source                | HUC parent recorded as                          |
|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| **PSGC (PSA)**        | the **region**                                  |
| **NAMRIA boundaries** | the **province** it sits geographically inside  |

A naive parent-lookup that joins NAMRIA polygons to PSGC by province would therefore misclassify
every HUC (e.g. place Makati under Rizal Province instead of NCR).
:::

## How this dataset resolves it

The script `generate_huc_mapping.py` produces
[`namria/huc_adm2_mapping.json`](https://github.com/bendlikeabamboo/barangay-boundaries-repository/blob/main/namria/huc_adm2_mapping.json),
an explicit lookup from each HUC to its correct PSGC parent. This mapping is consumed by:

- `coverage.py` — so coverage stats count HUCs correctly.
- `enrich.py` — so each HUC feature gets the right `psgc_code` and parent.

## Metro Manila: virtual provinces

Metro Manila (NCR) has **no PSGC province-level units** — it is regions → cities → barangays
directly. NAMRIA, however, publishes the four **NCR legislative districts** as ADM2 polygons. To
reconcile, this dataset maps those districts as **virtual provinces** of type `mm_district`:

| NAMRIA feature                    | Mapped type                       |
|-----------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Metropolitan Manila First District  | `mm_district` (virtual province) |
| Metropolitan Manila Second District | `mm_district` (virtual province) |
| Metropolitan Manila Third District  | `mm_district` (virtual province) |
| Metropolitan Manila Fourth District | `mm_district` (virtual province) |

These four features appear in `non_administrative.geojson` because they are not standard PSGC
provinces — they are documented honestly rather than silently dropped.

## Match confidence

Because HUCs require special handling, enriched features carry a `match_confidence` value
(`exact` / `huc_map` / `fuzzy`) — see [feature properties](../boundaries/properties.qmd).

For the 2023-10-24 snapshot, 31 of 34 HUCs matched exactly, 1 via the HUC map, and 2 via fuzzy
matching.
